title: Conservation of Energy
body:
**Conservation of energy** states that the total mechanical energy of a system stays constant
while only conservative forces act on it.

$$
KE_i + U_i = KE_f + U_f
$$

The method is to evaluate the total at two moments and equate them, with everything between
them ignored.

```
An object dropped from 5 m. How fast when it lands?

  start:  U = mgh,  KE = 0
  end:    U = 0,    KE = ½mv²

  mgh = ½mv²        the mass cancels
  v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 9.8 × 5) = 9.9 m/s
```

The mass cancelling is why every object dropped from that height arrives at that speed, and the
path never entered the calculation, so a bead sliding down any frictionless wire from 5 m
arrives at 9.9 m/s regardless of the shape of the wire. Solving that with
[[Newton's Laws]] would require knowing the normal force at every point.

[[Friction]] and other non-conservative forces break the equality, and the repair is to add
their [[Work]] to the balance:

$$
KE_i + U_i + W_{\text{friction}} = KE_f + U_f
$$

with $W_{\text{friction}}$ negative. The energy is not destroyed, it leaves the mechanical
account as heat, which is the direction the rest of physics develops from here.
